title: In 1960, Mathematicians Predicted that Earth’s Population Would Reach Infinity on a Friday Next Month - Nautilus
gist: A 1960 Science paper by Heinz von Foerster and colleagues extrapolated two millennia of hyperbolic population growth to predict human population would reach infinity on Friday, November 13, 2026; a new Science essay by UC Santa Barbara economist Javier Birchenall revisits what the forecast got wrong and right.

insights.claim: A 1960 paper in Science predicted that the human population would reach infinity on Friday, November 13, 2026, leading to the extinction of humankind.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A cautionary benchmark for long-range demographic extrapolation that underpins many macro forecasts.
insights.quote: the rapidly exploding human population would reach infinity on Friday, November 13, 2026, resulting in the extinction of humankind
insights.locator: In 1960, a paper published in Science

insights.claim: Von Foerster and colleagues built their 1960 doomsday forecast by modeling hyperbolic population growth fitted to the previous two millennia of data.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Shows how fitting a curve to historical trend data can produce spectacularly wrong predictions when regimes change.
insights.quote: who modeled future hyperbolic growth based on the last two millennia of data
insights.locator: In 1960, a paper published in Science

insights.claim: The 1960 authors argued that humanity's doom would come not from resource scarcity but from overcrowding, writing that future generations would be 'squeezed to death' rather than starve.
insights.speaker: Heinz von Foerster et al.
insights.so_what: An early dissent from Malthusian resource-scarcity framing that still colours population debates.
insights.quote: “Our great-great-grandchildren will not starve to death,” mathematician Heinz von Foerster et al. wrote. “They will be squeezed to death.”
insights.locator: In 1960, a paper published in Science

insights.claim: The predicted population apocalypse of November 2026 has evidently not occurred, falsifying the 1960 hyperbolic growth forecast.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Real-world population growth decelerated, breaking the historical hyperbolic trend that the model assumed.
